turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I'm having a real problem at work. I manage construction sites, and... lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or any kind of upper platform, my head just tells me I’m about to go over the edge. 

It doesn't even make sense to me, because I can look right at it and see the rails are in place, and I know the setup is supposed to be completely safe, but... the feeling is just there anyway. I just can't shake it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an intense, irrational fear of falling when near scaffolds or roof edges, despite knowing the setup is safe and rails are in place.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient states that this feeling of being about to go over the edge happens 'every time' they get near an upper platform, indicating an immediate anxiety response to the specific situation.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your reaction to being at heights, do you find yourself feeling constantly worried or anxious about many other different things in your daily life?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I have normal stress, like dealing with schedules or material delays on the site, but... no, I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person in general. It's really just this one specific thing with being up high. Outside of that, I feel completely fine.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient reiterates having a specific fear of being up high.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies being an anxious person in general or worrying constantly about other things in daily life.
